{{Short description|Belgian logician and philosopher (1889-1961)}}

'''Robert Feys''' (19 December 1889 – 13 April 1961) was a [[Belgians|Belgian]] [[logician]] and [[philosopher]], who worked at the [[Catholic University of Leuven (1834–1968)|University of Leuven]] ([[Belgium]]).<ref name="LDR 1961">De Raeymaeker, Louis. "[http://www.persee.fr/web/revues/home/prescript/article/phlou_0035-3841_1961_num_59_62_5080 In memoriam le chanoine Robert Feys]." ''Revue Philosophique de Louvain'' 59.62 (1961): 371-374.</ref>

Feys was born in [[Mechelen]],<ref name="LDR 1961"/> and received his PhD in 1909 from the [[Institute of Philosophy, University of Leuven]]. In 1913 he was appointed Professor at the [[Saint-Louis University, Brussels|Université Saint-Louis, Brussels]]. But due to the War he enlisted in the Army. In 1919 he was appointed Professor at the Institute St. Gertrude in [[Nivelles]]. In 1929 he returned to the Université Saint-Louis, Brussels, and in 1944 he was appointed Professor at the University of Leuven.<ref name="LDR 1961"/>

In 1958 Feys and [[Haskell B. Curry]] devised the [[type inference]] algorithm for the [[simply typed lambda calculus]] (''Combinatory Logic'').

== Selected publications ==
* [[Haskell B. Curry]], Robert Feys, and [[William Craig (philosopher)|William Craig]]. ''Combinatory Logic.'' Amsterdam, North-Holland Pub. Co., 1958–72. {{ISBN|0-7204-2208-6}}
* Robert Feys, ''Dictionary of Symbols of Mathematical Logic.'' Amsterdam : North-Holland Pub. Co., 1973, 1969. 

'''French'''
* Feys, Robert. "Les logiques nouvelles des modalités." ''Revue néo-scolastique de philosophie'' 40.56 (1937): 517–553.
* Feys, Robert. "Les systèmes formalisés des modalités aristotéliciennes." ''Revue philosophique de Louvain'', 48.20 (1950): 478–509.
* Feys, Robert. Étude géologique du Carbonifère briançonnais (Hautes-Alpes), 1957. Vol. 6. ''Éditions Technip'', 1963.
